headline: Approved National Grid easement for anchor and guy wires to secure a leaning pole on Forest Street.
summary: Members said they would not have supported the easement on their own, but granted it because a pole on Forest Street was leaning dangerously. Separately, the group voted to update the cemetery handbook, which had not been updated since 2017, and to make the president a voting member.

plain_text:
MEETING MINUTES OF: October 21, 2026
A meeting of the Cemetery Board of Trustees was held at the Forest Dale Cemetery, 150 Forest Street, Malden on 
the above date, in accordance with the Notice of Meeting, as provided in G.L. c.30A,§§ 18-25. Notice was filed with 
the City Clerk’s Office, City of Malden.
President James Tuxbury called the meeting to order at 5:00 P.M. Members present were James Tuxbury, Vincent 
Miraglia, Joseph Barriss, Sheila Fermano and Superintendent Chris Rosa.
APPROVAL OF MINUTES: The minutes of the September 16, 2026 meeting were read and upon the motion of 
Vincent Miraglia and seconded by Joseph Barriss, the Board voted to accept the minutes as read; all were in favor. 
CARRIED
The minutes of the September 25, 2026 meeting were read and upon the motion of Joseph Barriss and seconded 
by Vincent Miraglia, the Board voted to accept the minutes as read; all were in favor. CARRIED
Motion was made by Vincent Miraglia and seconded by Joseph Barriss to rescind the motion to approve the 
minutes from the September 25, 2026 meeting due to information provided to the Board from the State Ethics 
Commission regarding the Conflict of Interest Laws; all were in favor. CARRIED
CORRESPONDENCE: None
TREASURER REPORT: Cemetery Superintendent Chris Rosa provided the following information: The Cemetery 
Trust received income for the month of September in the amount of $19,587.36 for Perpetual Care. This money 
was turned over to the Treasurer’s office to be added to the Cemetery Trust accounts. Upon the motion of Sheila 
Fermano and seconded Joseph Barriss, the Board voted to accept the Trust Report as read; all were in favor. 
CARRIED
SUPERINTENDENT’S REPORT: The Superintendent’s report was received by the Trustees. Superintendent Rosa 
provided the following information: Burials for the month of September were as follows: 2 (two) existing full body 
burials; one (1) new Veteran’s grave and eight (8) existing lot cremains for a total of eleven (11)) burials.
 Superintendent Rosa stated twenty (20) new double deep graves were installed in Section 1C and twenty 
(20) more would be coming next week, thus completing the project.
 The front gate will be repaired by the end of this week.
 Twenty (20) new trees have been planted.
 A new dump insert has been purchased and will be installed on Monday.
 Repairs to the Cemetery House are scheduled for the first week in November.
 Phone and internet service is in the process of being upgraded through a different provider.
 Veterans Day will be held at Forest Dale Cemetery this year.
 Wreaths Across America will be at Forest Dale Cemetery Saturday, December 19th (second year).
The motion to accept Superintendent’s report was made by Joseph Barriss and seconded by Vincent Miraglia; all 
were in favor. CARRIED
OLD BUSINESS: Much discussion on the proposed easement from National Grid (NG) for the installation of 
anchors and guy wires within the cemetery. President Tuxbury reminded the members at a meeting held in late 
spring, the Trustees approved National Grid’s request for anchors and guy wire placement at a specific location 
provided NG contacted the Superintendent prior to entering the cemetery with equipment due to the possibility of 
interrupting funerals.  It was noted during discussion that NG had not adhered to the provisions as stated by the 
James Tuxbury, President
Sheila L. Fermano, Secretary
Joseph Barris, Trustee
Vincent Miraglia, Trustee
TRUSTEES of CEMETERIES
City of Malden
150 Forest Street, Malden, MA 02148
781-322-2360
Trustees and were forced by the Superintendent to leave the premises due to an ongoing funeral. The 
Superintendent brought forward the proposed easement due to the immediate need of anchor/guy wire support for 
a pole on Forest Street leaning over dangerously and in need of support ASAP. Much discussion among the 
Trustees against the proposed easement and all agreed if it was left up to the Trustees, the proposal would not be 
supported. However, due to the urgency of the leaning pole, a motion was made by Vincent Miraglia and seconded 
by Joseph Barriss to grant the request from National Grid for an easement to install anchor and guy wires to secure
existing sidewalk poles; all were in favor. CARRIED
President Tuxbury told the Trustees he would request to appear before the City Council when they considered the 
easement paper and would provide them with the Trustees input and concerns within the cemetery.
NEW BUSINESS: Motion was made by Sheila Fermano and seconded by Vincent Miraglia to update the Cemetery
Handbook; all were in favor. CARRIED (NOTE: handbook had not been updated since 2017.)
Motion was made by Vincent Miraglia and seconded by Joseph Barriss to approve and authorize the President to 
be a voting member of the Trustees; all were in favor. CARRIED
GENERAL CEMETERY BUSINESS: Trustees instructed the Superintendent to remove ornamentation that was not
allowed in the Veterans Section prior to Veterans Day.
Next meeting of the Board of Trustees: The next meeting of the Cemetery Board of Trustees will be held on 
Thursday, November 19, 2026 at 5:00 PM.
ADJOURMENT: All business before the Board of Trustees having been completed and upon motion of Vincent 
Miraglia and seconded by Joseph Barriss, the meeting was adjourned at 6:00 P.M.
Respectfully submitted,
Sheila Fermano, Secretary
